subject: Bamboo coral
topic: This coral, almost as big as NOAA's robot, could be hundreds of years old.
script:
This coral, almost as big as NOAA's robot, could be hundreds of years old.
It's a bamboo coral, named for its jointed skeleton that looks like bamboo.
Its branches are made of hard, stony sections joined by flexible ones.
That lets it bend in deep-sea currents without snapping.
Like tree rings, its skeleton grows in layers that scientists can use to study the ocean's past.
Off the southeastern US, NOAA found a two-meter bamboo coral shaped like a candelabra.
Scientists think it may belong to a group no one has named yet.
Others grow as single, long whips, rising straight up toward passing food.
Which one would you want to name?
